title: Attentional blink (Raymond, Shapiro & Arnell, 1992, Experiment 2)
summary: Letters flash one at a time at 11 per second. Subjects identify the one white letter and then say whether a black X followed it, or, in a control condition, ignore the white letter and only look for the X. Detecting the X drops for about half a second after the target only when the target has to be identified: the attentional blink. One trial is one stream and one or two reports.
references: Raymond, J. E., Shapiro, K. L., & Arnell, K. M. (1992). Temporary suppression of visual processing in an RSVP task: An attentional blink? Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance, 18(3), 849-860. https://doi.org/10.1037/0096-1523.18.3.849

deviations.original: Spoken: the subject named the white letter and said whether an X was present; an experimenter, blind to the correct answers, entered them on a second computer (pp. 851, 853)
deviations.here: Typed by the subject: the white letter on the letter keys, then Y or N for the X
deviations.reason: No experimenter transcription in alhazen; unspeeded reports after the stream measure the same thing without a transcription step

deviations.original: The subject pressed the mouse button when ready (p. 852)
deviations.here: The subject presses SPACE when ready
deviations.reason: Keyboard-only rig; the same self-paced start

deviations.original: Macintosh II and Apple 13-in monitor: letters 15 ms on, 75 ms grey ISI, 11.11 letters/s (p. 851)
deviations.here: Whole frames of the rig's refresh rate, the 90 ms SOA kept first (120 Hz: 16.7 ms on, 75.0 ms off, SOA 91.7 ms; 100 and 200 Hz: SOA 90.0 ms). Realised durations are recorded on every trial; run mode refuses a rate outside the tolerances (60 Hz: SOA 83.3 ms)
deviations.reason: A modern display cannot show 15 ms at most refresh rates

deviations.original: One-minute rest every 60 trials; a longer rest permitted between conditions (p. 853)
deviations.here: alhazen's block-break screen after every 60 trials, after practice and between conditions, ended by SPACE; the minute is asked for in the instructions, not enforced
deviations.reason: alhazen's breaks are self-paced; the operator can time the minute

deviations.here: A ready screen before each trial (a one-line reminder of the condition; the full condition instructions on its first trial) and a prompt for each typed report
deviations.reason: Typed responses need prompts, and the subject must know which condition is running

deviations.here: A report not given within 30 s, or a trial not started within 10 min, is recorded (NO_RESPONSE / NO_START) and the trial is served again later in its block
deviations.reason: alhazen's re-serve rule keeps the planned counts

tasks.title: Attentional blink: experimental and control conditions
tasks.summary: SPACE starts a trial; a white dot for 180 ms; then an RSVP stream of black letters (15 ms on, 75 ms off) with one white target after 7-15 letters and 8 letters after it, an X on half the trials at serial position 0..+8; then the reports.
tasks.description: One session runs both conditions in the counterbalanced order, each as 10 practice trials and 180 trials in three blocks of 60. Experimental: type the white letter, then Y/N for the X. Control: Y/N for the X only. Probe detection is analysed by serial position, for experimental trials with the target correct.
